narrative_summary: The S&P 500 broke to a fresh all-time high at 7,758.21 and closed at 7,736.52, a sixth straight advancing session that walks the upper Bollinger Band and lifts extension to +9.98% above the 200-day. Monte Carlo has flipped to its most constructive skew of the arc (69.76% up-first, median 2 days to the swing high) but still fails the 70% Late Bull threshold, and rally exhaustion was upgraded to Moderate. Against that, internals are the weakest of the entire sequence relative to price: McClellan breadth sits near its cycle-low shelf, net new 52-week highs are at 1.06, 5-day MFI has rolled from ~91 down to ~78 into the new high, the daily close landed in the bottom third of the range, and ERP is pinned at 0.28% inside the valuation-ceiling band. This is a textbook late-cycle melt-up: hold core, harvest trims into 7,700-7,760 strength, and wait for the 7,588/7,536 fib shelf or the 7,481 50-day to do the work before any re-entry.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: McClellan summation has turned modestly up off its recent low (908.66 vs ~830 trough) and net new 52-week highs remain positive at 1.06, so participation is not collapsing while price makes new highs.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: A new all-time high accompanied by a McClellan reading sitting on its cycle-low reference line and net new highs compressed to 1.06 (score 30) is narrow leadership — falling or flat participation at new highs is a classic topping warning.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: When breadth and credit both diverge from price, elevate caution even if price has not yet broken down; headline strength with weak breadth indicates narrow leadership.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: MFI at ~78 on the 5-day and ~62 on the 1-month chart is still comfortably above 50, so money flow remains net positive and has simply cooled from an extreme.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: Price made a higher high (7,758.21) while 5-day MFI made a lower high (~91 down to ~78) and intraday RSI collapsed from ~85 to ~30 into a bottom-third close — a bearish money-flow divergence at the very moment of breakout, the signature of distribution into strength.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: Bearish divergence: price makes a higher high while MFI or RSI makes a lower high. Trim zone: RSI above 70, MFI above 80. Report where the close occurred within the daily range.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: Adjusted prob_up_first of 69.76% with a 2-day median to the upside target and an 88% cascade to 7,855 clears the 65% Early/Mid Bull bar and argues the path of least resistance is still higher.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: Under Late Bull / Topping the required threshold is 70%, so 69.76% fails by a hair — a ninth consecutive session without an actionable edge — and the exhaustion score has been upgraded to Moderate, which mandates discounting upside probabilities.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: If the adjusted probability does not meet the threshold for that regime, the setup is not actionable. Never use the Monte Carlo output in isolation.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: Forward EPS keeps rising (380) and a 10-year that has eased to 4.627% from 4.745% holds forward PE at a merely-cautious 20.36x, so the valuation ceiling is being lifted by fundamentals rather than breached.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: ERP of 0.28% is inside the 0.0-0.5% valuation-ceiling band with a stable trend and the ERP-confirmed re-entry floor at 7,411.74 — 4.2% below spot — meaning equities offer essentially no premium over risk-free yield at this price.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: ERP 0.0% to 0.5% = valuation ceiling: trim bias, no aggressive adds. Forward PE 20x-22x = cautious buying only at strong confluence.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: At +9.98% above the 200-day the market is only moderately extended, well short of the 15%+ extreme zone, and the drift path still projects 7,846.88 at 60 days.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: Extension has jumped from +8.13% to +9.98% in one session and sits at the boundary of the elevated 10-15% band, where the framework mandates meaningfully reduced drift and elevated mean-reversion pressure — six vertical sessions off 7,313.92 is velocity, not accumulation.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: 10% to 15% above the 200-day = elevated extension and meaningfully reduced drift; classify move magnitude, velocity, and volatility compression before interpreting the simulation.

conflicting_evidence.bullish_read: VIX at 16.50 sits mid-band with the junk spread at a one-year tight, and the absence of stress means there is no forced-selling overhang to fight the advance.
conflicting_evidence.bearish_read: The 7/29 low that launched this move never produced a 25-30 VIX capitulation spike (peak 20.66), so the rally is built on an orderly dip rather than a washed-out low; VIX also ticked up 15.86 to 16.50 on a new-high day, and put/call at 0.75 shows no complacency-driven fuel either.
conflicting_evidence.framework_rule: A correction that unfolds without a volatility spike should be treated as orderly rather than capitulative; a VIX spike into 25-30 followed by reversal is the high-quality re-entry signal.

primary_tension: A record-setting, upper-band-walking advance with the strongest Monte Carlo up-skew of the arc (69.76% up-first) and the tightest credit spreads of the year is colliding with the weakest internal confirmation of the entire sequence: McClellan breadth near its 908.66 cycle-low shelf and net new 52-week highs at 1.06 as price makes new all-time highs, 5-day MFI rolling from ~91 to ~78 into the high, a bottom-third daily close with intraday RSI collapsing from ~85 to ~30, extension stretched to +9.98% above the 200-day, rally exhaustion upgraded to Moderate, ERP pinned at 0.28% inside the valuation-ceiling band, and the Monte Carlo edge still failing the 70% Late Bull threshold for a ninth consecutive session.
